The programme / From question to creation

Four months.
A world to explore.

A small cohort, a steady rhythm, and four connected labs. Children learn by encountering the world, asking questions, making things, and trying again.

16 weeks3 days a week5 learning hours a day12 children maximum

The journey, month by month.

Four weeks in each lab. New questions throughout.

Month01

Design & Engineering

Build with matter.

Children investigate movement, structure, materials, and mechanisms. They make ideas tangible, test what happens, and improve their work. The month moves towards building something for someone else.

MoveStandTransformBuild for someone
Month02

Futures

Build possibilities.

Children explore what could be different and imagine possible worlds. Ideas take shape as models and prototypes, making room to ask what a better future could look like—and who it might help.

ImagineExplore possibilitiesPrototype
Month03

Culture

Build how we live together.

Children explore the foundations of community: shared life, belonging, and the choices people make together. They consider how their actions and creations can help a community flourish.

BelongingCommunityCare
Month04

Media

Build meaning.

Children develop thinking, language, and storytelling. They turn experiences and ideas into stories, practise communicating clearly, and prepare to share what they have made and learned.

ThinkTell storiesShare

A programme overview. Detailed sessions and learning materials will be added to the curriculum.

A rhythm for discovery

Encounter. Make.
Reflect. Repeat.

Each learning day holds five hours for guided exploration, sustained making, practice, and shared life. Teaching is in English, with up to five adults supporting the cohort.

Questions open the work. Making gives children something to test. Reflection helps them see what changed—and why.

  1. 01

    Encounter & wonder

    Look closely, touch materials, ask questions, and make an initial guess.

  2. 02

    Make, test & change

    Try an idea, notice what happens, and use the result to improve it.

  3. 03

    Explain & practise

    Share the thinking. Return regularly to the speedcube, abacus, and spatial reasoning.

  4. 04

    The Village

    A daily, one-hour block embedded in the programme for community, responsibility, and learning to live well together.

The work comes together

A story of learning.
Something worth sharing.

Across the cohort, children create individual pieces of work and contribute to a collective build. The programme culminates in a Builders Assembly—a moment to share their creations, explain their thinking, and reflect on the journey.

A few practical things

Good questions
to start with.

Who is the programme for?

The cohort is for children aged 5–9. Mixed-age learning brings children together within one deliberately selected group, with a maximum of 12 children.

How much time does it involve?

The programme runs for four months: four labs of four weeks each. Children attend three days a week, with five learning hours each day. Exact dates and weekly meeting days will be shared separately.

Will there be homework?

There is no homework. Home practice guides support continued exploration with each child’s own speedcube, abacus, and spatial kit.

What carries across all four labs?

The speedcube, abacus, and spatial reasoning recur across all 16 weeks. The daily Village block continues throughout, alongside individual work and the collective build.

Where can I see the full curriculum?

The curriculum page currently contains the programme outline. Detailed learning materials will be added as they are developed. View the curriculum page →
